sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 sits near the top of its one-month range (7,706, about 72% of the band, vs. a one-month high of 7,765) while the Nasdaq 100 is effectively at a one-month high (30,470, 99% of range, high 30,482). The Euro Stoxx 50 is the outlier, near the bottom of its own one-month range (6,300, about 26% of range, low 6,236). The VIX is subdued at 15.2, near the low end of its one-month range (24%) — no volatility stress showing in US options pricing. Against that backdrop, 27 SP500/R1000/isCore operating names report this week, concentrated in industrials (5 names), financial-services (6 names), and consumer-cyclical (6 names).

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon: JEF US reports into financial-services, median +0.19% recently — modest but positive. Tue: UAL US reports into industrials, the week's most negative sector tilt at -1.42% median across 627 names. Wed: MU US reports into technology, the strongest positive tilt among heavily-reported sectors at +0.87% median. Thu: AYI US adds a second industrials print. Fri: KO US closes the week into consumer-defensive, median -0.54%.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the sector reaction table at +6.62% median across 176 tickers, backed by a thick 2,630-item news window — the most-confirmed signal on the board. Alternative-asset-management (+2.93%, 6 tickers, 240 items) and copper (+2.63%, 6 tickers, 248 items) follow but on much thinner coverage, so weight those two with more caution than mining's breadth.
